## Task 1: Load packages and generate the dataset

```{r load-packages}
library(tidyverse)
library(skimr)
```

```{r task1-generate}
options(bdat602.source_only = TRUE)
source("courses/bdat-602/_teacher/resources/datasets/simulate_bdat602_data.R")

health_data <- simulate_bdat602(n = 500000, seed = 602)
dim(health_data)  # should print 500000 40
```

## Task 2: CRISP-DM Phase 1 — Business Understanding for fraud detection

```{r task2-business-understanding}
# Business problem:
#   The insurer processes ~50,000 claims per month. An estimated 3% are fraudulent,
#   costing the company roughly $2M annually. Manual review of all claims is not scalable.

# Mining objective:
#   Build a binary classifier on fraud_flag using claim_amount, num_claims,
#   employment_type, weekend_claim, and age to score each new claim.

# Success criterion:
#   Recall >= 0.75 on the test set (we prefer to investigate genuine fraud even
#   if it means some false positives). Precision >= 0.40 to keep the investigation
#   team's workload manageable.

# Data source:
#   simulate_bdat602() with n = 500,000. fraud_flag prevalence is ~3%.

# Constraints:
#   Must not use record_id or policyholder_id as features.
#   Model must be auditable (no black-box approaches without explanation).
```

## Task 3: Explore the three target variables

```{r task3-targets-skim}
health_data |>
  select(churned, high_risk, claim_amount) |>
  skim()
```

```{r task3-plot}
health_data |>
  filter(claim_amount > 0) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = claim_amount)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 60, fill = "steelblue", colour = "white") +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::dollar) +
  labs(
    title = "Distribution of Claim Amounts (non-zero claims only)",
    x = "Claim Amount (USD)",
    y = "Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()

# Distribution shape:
# The distribution is strongly right-skewed: the bulk of claims are below $10,000
# but a long tail extends to $80,000+. This suggests a log transformation will
# be needed before regression modelling.
```

```{r task3-churn-rate}
churn_rate    <- mean(health_data$churned,    na.rm = TRUE)
high_risk_rate <- mean(health_data$high_risk, na.rm = TRUE)

cat("Churn rate:    ", round(churn_rate * 100, 1), "%\n")
cat("High-risk rate:", round(high_risk_rate * 100, 1), "%\n")

# high_risk has higher prevalence (~40%) than churned (~18%).
# churned is more imbalanced and will need SMOTE or class weighting (Module 5).
```

## Task 4: Spark connection (eval=FALSE)

```{r task4-spark, eval=FALSE}
library(sparklyr)

sc <- spark_connect(master = "local[*]", version = "3.4.1")

health_tbl <- copy_to(sc, health_data, name = "health_insurance", overwrite = TRUE)

plan_counts <- health_tbl |>
  count(plan_tier) |>
  collect()

print(plan_counts)

spark_disconnect(sc)
```
